prompts: Shot 1 opens with a black screen followed by a fade-in, wide overhead composition: foreground features pine branches bent by sea wind, midground shows rocky ground at the forest edge, background faintly reveals gray sea and cable car lines. Deep depth of field clearly establishes environmental relationships. An elderly gray-haired male and his partner slowly circle each other at half-step distance. The elder bends knees, lowers center of gravity, extends hands forward to test distance. His shoes lightly press gravel, causing subtle shifts, while jacket flaps are lifted sideways by the wind. The camera performs a slight downward tilt and slow push-in.

Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, close-up eye-level angle where subjects dominate the frame, background blurred into dark green coniferous trees and gray-white sea. Composition focuses on shoulder lines, forearms, and chest contact zones. The partner suddenly grabs and drives in, the elder smoothly engages, drops hips to secure inner control, one forearm pressing against opponent’s torso midline, the other hand gripping upper limb to form a frame, body center steadily pushing forward. Natural light grazes facial and arm textures from behind and side, sweat and fabric wrinkles preserved with low contrast. Camera makes small lateral pan following grappling motion.

Shot 3 enters via a hard cut into an extreme close-up eye-level shot. Shallow depth of field focuses attention on footwork and arm control. Blurred foreground pants and elbows create leading lines, focus locked on the elder’s foot entering, sweeping action, and hand controlling partner’s upper arm. Pants, hem, and cuffs flick briefly due to rotation. Camera performs short horizontal follow-move with slight downward tilt, clarifying direction of sweep and hip turn.

Shot 4 connects via matching edit based on continuous motion, medium-close shot panning down to pebble beach below. Left side retains slope and sparse tree shadows, right side shows wet stones and gray sea waves. Environmental transition aligns naturally with post-throw landing, avoiding abruptness. Upon landing, the elder immediately presses in, quickly adjusts knee and hip alignment, transitions into stable side control, then applies shoulder pressure to form shoulder lock. Partner attempts to find gaps but remains blocked. Lighting maintains overcast seaside quality, only faint cold reflections appear on wet stones. Camera performs low-amplitude lateral pan along ground level, reinforcing continuity from throw to ground control. Landing thud coincides with a heavier guitar strum. Afterward,

Shot 5 cuts hard from previous shot, low-angle close-up with slow push-in. Behind subjects, sky appears wind-blown white, diagonal pine branch enters frame. Focus shifts from elder’s tensed forearm to his controlled expression and space beside partner’s neck. During ground control, he smoothly repositions, arms slide in to form rear-naked choke structure, but does not tighten. Immediately after confirming control, he reduces force and releases—action clearly demonstrating training restraint and safety boundaries. Partner taps to signal release and relaxes. Side-backlight gently highlights hair strands, earlobes, and forearm contours, face still maintains low saturation and low contrast realistic texture. Push-in pace synchronizes with guitar’s closing phrase.

Shot 6 connects via soft fade-in cut from previous shot, wide pull-out. Camera retreats from beside subjects to higher, farther position, reintegrating pebble beach, slope, coniferous forest, and sea into single frame. Foreground features grass stems pushed by wind, subjects recede to mid-ground lower area forming stable concluding composition. Jacket hems and pants legs continuously flutter in sea wind. Body tension gradually shifts from confrontation to post-training relaxation. Camera steadily pulls back, allowing environment to reclaim human actions. Low saturation cool tone remains consistent.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in from black, using a long shot overhead view. The clock tower spire is positioned at the upper third of the frame, with a copper pointer sliced by rain in the foreground, and layered gear towers and steam conduits extending into the distance in the background, creating deep vertical depth. Rain makes the spire gleam; a girl child stands on the narrow tip, body slightly crouched, arms drawn in, toes pressing against the wet metal edge. Her cloak hem and hair are whipped sideways by strong wind, creating a sense of compressed anticipation.

Shot 2 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium-long shot from a low angle. After leaping from the spire, the girl grabs the cable and slides through the air, her body pulled into a long arc by momentum. Her shoes skim through mist, her clothing flares in high-speed airflow, and the taut cable visibly vibrates. Raindrops are sliced open ahead of her, forming a fan-shaped pattern.

Shot 3 transitions from the previous shot via continuity motion cut, entering a wide shot at eye level with a slight downward angle. A large slowly rotating gear edge appears in the foreground, while staggered gear platforms in the midground resemble moving stairs leading forward. In the background, steam pipes intersect into a three-dimensional grid. She leans forward lightly, uses core strength to flip like wirework, narrowly avoiding a lateral burst of high-pressure steam just before it erupts. White vapor explodes behind her. The action shifts from vertical descent to horizontal traversal. Steam hissing suddenly pierces through the rain in The camera performs lateral pan with slight orbiting, capturing the layering of gear meshing and agile evasion.

Shot 4 transitions from the previous shot via a hard cut after steam obscures the scene, shifting to a close-up at eye level. A copper railing diagonally crosses from bottom-left to top-right, with shallow depth of field blurring the background gears into flowing light spots. As she flips down, her fingertips brush the wet copper railing, leaving a trail of tiny water droplets and spark-like reflections on the metal surface. Her toe finally lands firmly on the narrow foothold, bringing her from near imbalance to full control.

Shot 5 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, changing to a medium side-angle high-angle shot. A long pipe extends from the bottom of the frame toward the distant reactor, with occasional steam valves passing through the foreground to create speed obstruction. Tower lights in the background are stretched into lines by rain. The girl sprints along the wet pipe, her stride rapid and stable, kicking up splashes with each step. As several sharp metal shards are blown toward her by the wind, she uses the momentum from a solid step to leap and spin-kick. Her leg draws a sharp arc, shattering the first shard head-on, sending fragments scattering and reflecting in the rain. Other shards are deflected by the impact. The action completes a full burst from running to jumping to striking.

Shot 6 transitions from the previous shot via a flying debris blocking the frame, cutting to a medium-close high-angle shot. Dense rain occupies the foreground, a taut steel cable suddenly enters from outside the frame. In the midground, the girl’s body is violently pulled upward. In the background, steam vents and flickering furnace light are visible. Her waist is lifted by inertia, her body spins rapidly mid-air, rain trailing arcs from her limbs. For half a second at the peak of ascent, she executes a powerful back kick using core strength, her heel slicing through the rain curtain. The cable, cloak, and hair show brief physical lag before being torn apart again by wind. The camera performs a half-orbit slow-motion follow, then abruptly freezes the suspension moment.

Shot 7 transitions from the previous shot via a soft fade-in with dynamic momentum buffer, settling into a long shot from behind and above. The core reactor's top is centered in the frame, with the mechanical city below spreading out like a vast copper maze. Steam plumes and rotating towers unfold layer by layer in the rainy night, creating extreme depth. The girl finally lands steadily on the reactor top, knees slightly bent to absorb impact, then rises upright. Her silhouette is clearly defined against the backlight. She overlooks the roaring mechanical city, concluding the series of explosive actions. Water droplets roll off the edge of the reactor beside her, while distant gears continue turning—creating a contrast between stillness and motion. The camera slowly pulls back and gently ascends, framing her together with the entire city, ending on a grand scale.

prompts: Shot 1 begins directly with a wide-angle upward composition that includes the subway entrance, glowing signage, and receding lines of the passage. The foreground features slightly blurred railings, while focus rests on a big-eyed sprite leaping onto the signboard. Low-saturation blue-purple neon outlines it from behind, and high-contrast side lighting highlights its rounded facial contours and ear tips. After landing lightly on the edge, it performs two ear-shaking warm-ups, shoulders and knees bouncing gently to the synth intro, with noticeable delayed sway in its ear tips and small cape. The camera slowly pushes in and tilts up slightly.

Shot 2 hard-cuts from the previous shot to the concourse turnstile area, using a close-up eye-level tracking shot. The turnstiles form strong leading lines, with occasional blue indicator lights and transparent barriers passing through the foreground. Focus remains locked on the sprite moving between turnstiles. Blue-purple neon and side lighting are maintained, with only faint cyan glow reflected from the turnstile screens.

The escalator’s light strips and metal edges form a diagonal composition. Background crowds and steps are deliberately blurred into flowing textures. Cold neon continues to dominate, with side lighting outlining the tail’s edge. It performs continuous hip swings in time with the descending escalator, its tail swaying almost in sync with the side light strips. Ear tips bounce lightly with head tapping, weight shifting constantly between left and right feet. Each staccato note of the synthesized piano matches the tail’s swing amplitude. The camera subtly pitches and follows with minor movement, transitioning from detailed motion to more pronounced rhythmic escalation.

Shot 4 transitions via a brief fade cut to the platform, using a near-medium eye-level push-in. Train light strips approach from afar, creating depth pressure. Platform edges and safety lines naturally guide attention to the subject. Focus centers on the sprite poised in the middle of the platform. The base tone remains blue-purple neon, but the approaching train adds white cool light overlapping with side lighting. Wind pressure lifts both its small cape and ears. It lowers its center of gravity, pulls hands back, then uses the moment of train arrival to perform a rapid spin. The camera continues pushing in with slight orbiting, emphasizing the turning point and climax.

Shot 5 hard-cuts from the previous shot to a low-angle close-up before the train doors. The foreground features slightly blurred door frame edges. Focus is sharply locked on the point where the sprite’s toes meet the ground. Lighting maintains cold neon and strong side lighting, with only brief flashes from the warning light near the feet. It enters its fastest sequence of quick steps: toes, heels, soles landing in succession. Upper body appears only partially with minimal arm swing at the edges. Emphasis is on lower-body power and continuous rhythmic division. Each step lands precisely on the warning chime and mechanical door bell cues. The camera performs very short lateral slides and micro-pushes, enhancing the speed perception of fragmented steps.

Shot 6 enters the empty carriage via a match cut triggered by the door opening. Occasionally, a strap swings across the foreground. Focus remains stable on the sprite gripping the strap. Blue-purple neon filters through windows into the carriage, with side lighting clearly defining arm, face, and torso movements. It performs a full wave motion using the strap as leverage, transferring force from wrist to elbow, shoulder, chest, and down to hips and waist. The tail adds a soft delayed sway after the wave. The camera glides smoothly along the carriage’s length, creating a fluid mid-section extension.

Overhead lights and wall neon recede into a vanishing point. Foreground floor reflections gently elongate the subject’s silhouette. Focus rests on the sprite running toward the camera in the center of the corridor. The overall tone remains low-saturation blue-purple with high-contrast side lighting, with only a soft cool-white fill light appearing from the exit direction. Ears and cape retain slight inertial sway after the freeze. Background neon glow fades slowly, while synthesized tail notes, turnstile echoes, and keyboard mechanical remnants converge and end together. The camera continues pulling back, leaving the character frozen in the center of the corridor for a crisp, memorable ending.

Handheld lateral movement with slight forward push creates a sense of running urgency.

Leading lines converge from bridge supports and pavement edges toward an old road sign. The boy bursts into the center frame and quickly crouches, pulling a coin from his palm and pressing it into a hidden slot on the sign. Foreground includes his extended hand and glowing edge of the map; background features shadows under the bridge and distant moving pedestrians. Lighting maintains consistent golden hour glow with localized shadows. As the coin is pressed, the slot glows faintly. Then a crisp “咔哒” triggers the iron gate to open. The The camera performs a very slight downward tilt from overhead, reinforcing the certainty of activation.

Focus is on the boy’s open palm and an old key. Foreground is blurred damp wall texture; background features elongated light spots deep in the alley. Minimal neon side lighting casts cold-warm interwoven highlights on the key’s edge, but the overall scene remains wrapped in warm dusk tones. Light flickers across the key’s surface. The camera starts from a static close-up, then slowly zooms in before following him as he turns and sprints out of the alley. His jacket hem and backpack strap swing naturally with motion.

Composition uses circular paving stones to focus attention on his feet. As he stops and looks up, warm golden magical patterns emerge sequentially from cracks in the tiles, spreading outward from near to far, forming clear spatial layers. Golden hour light illuminates the entire square; water droplets refract faint warm glimmers. After a stable pan, the camera slightly tilts upward, guiding the viewer’s gaze toward the clock tower base.

The camera slowly pushes forward along the low-angle trajectory to an extreme close-up of fingers touching the glowing surface, concluding the film in stillness.

prompts: Shot 1 Opens with a direct hard cut to a wide eye-level shot. The composition uses the circular track of Gear Square and towering pipes to create strong leading lines. Two elderly women are positioned slightly left of the frame's center axis. In the foreground, iron railings and steam vents are struck by rain; in the background, massive gears turn slowly and the tower's light strips flicker on and off. Steam in the environment is backlit, revealing cold white edges. One elderly woman rushes quickly from the side of the track toward the other, leaning forward with arms sharply flung out. Her raincoat hem and scarf are lifted by the wind. At the moment their distance suddenly closes, she shouts, 'You sold the core valve again? The listener initially freezes, then jaw tightens and eyes lift upward. The vibration of the railway tracks in the background synchronizes with the impact of this accusation. The camera performs a slight forward push with a subtle rightward pan, pulling the conflict out of the environment.

Shot 2: Hard-cut transition to a close-up eye-level tracking shot. The two women are almost nose-to-nose, occupying left and right sides of frame. Shallow depth of field blurs neon and wheels behind steam into shimmering bokeh. Occasional raindrops streak across lens edges. Focus shifts tightly between their rain-soaked faces. The aggressor continues rapid questioning; the other immediately retorts “你没资格这样问我”. Tiny droplets of spittle briefly sparkle under side-backlight. Listener does not retreat, only pupils constrict and nostrils flare when interrupted. Wind and steam hisses leave minimal gaps between lines. Camera makes small lateral tracking motion along their sides, intensifying the claustrophobic confrontation.

The third shot enters with a more abrupt hard cut into a tight, eye-level close-up, framing only the trembling lips, taut nasolabial folds, and rain-soaked facial details of an elderly woman. The background is compressed into a cold, desaturated blur of metallic surface.

Shot 4: Quick whip cut to medium side-angle shot. Composition creates intersecting diagonal lines between their bodies. Foreground features damp pipe and drifting steam; background neon signs flicker intermittently through fog. Industrial lighting remains cold and neutral, but side-backlighting is more pronounced. The second woman finally grabs the other’s collar and yanks sideways, fabric creasing. The first instinctively raises shoulder to resist and grabs wrist. Their faces now angled toward each other, eyes locked with defiant refusal to yield. Camera performs fast short lateral pan from left to right, following the pull force, syncing action with swirling steam across frame.

prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, showing a wide overhead view of the stone pavilion on cloud platform and surrounding misty mountains. Stone railings, eaves, and distant misty bridge form layered leading lines. In the foreground, gauze and drooping branches flutter gently in the wind. In the midground, an elderly man with white beard stands before a table. The background features a hazy lotus pond and faint green mountain silhouettes. Soft light descends from above, focusing on the central bronze mirror and jade cup on the pavilion. The The camera performs a very slow downward tilt followed by a slight push-in, establishing spatial relationships between the mythical environment and experimental apparatus.

Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium eye-level shot that slowly pushes in. The composition uses the table as a horizontal axis. The elder’s hands, one in front and one behind, steadily manipulate the ancient bronze mirror and water-filled jade cup. Shallow depth of field blurs the misty background, focusing on the moment sunlight reflected from the mirror enters the cup. The water surface starts still, then develops small ripples, creating a soft, bright bent trajectory of refracted light in the air. A flickering highlight appears on bamboo scrolls and jade objects beside the table. The guqin continues playing; the wooden wheel The camera moves smoothly along the table axis, clearly showing the process of light entering the vessel.

Shot 3 cuts hard into a close-up eye-level shot, tightly framing the edge of the prism and the bronze mirror surface. The foreground shows a slightly bluish crystal facet, while the background is a blurred red wall. Focus shifts with the mirror’s angle to the dancing reflection spots on the wall. Under side lighting, fine oxidation textures on the mirror, prism edges, and the transformation of light spots—from scattered to concentrated and then lightly jumping—are meticulously recorded. The watercolor brushstroke texture makes highlights appear softly diffused like paint.

Shot 4 transitions from the previous shot via a soft dissolve, shifting to a close-up overhead view of the table. The jade cup, bronze mirror, prism, and the elder’s hands form a stable diagonal composition. Focus gradually shifts from fingers to the flowing caustic patterns on the tabletop. As the elder slowly rotates the mirror, ripples spread across the water in the cup, and caustic patterns glide over the wooden surface, curled bamboo scrolls, and blue-green jade paperweight like fish scales. The shape of the bright spots evolves from fragmented dots to sheet-like streaks, then re-converges. Lighting remains consistently natural daylight with side illumination. The camera performs a slight overhead circular pan and minor downward tilt, making the dynamic light patterns the absolute focal point.
Shot 5 cuts abruptly to a close-up, eye-level view, framing the elder's upper body and the object in his hands.

Shot 6 follows seamlessly with a tracking shot, following a chain of moving light spots away from the table. It first passes the edge of the pavilion, then glides over the railing of the misty bridge, finally landing on the lotus pond surface. The shot naturally transitions from medium to long-medium, maintaining a level perspective slightly low, forming rich depth with bridge shadows, railings, and water ripples as leading lines. Focus continuously tracks how the light spot changes across different materials: sharp and defined on the stone railing, softened in the mist beneath the bridge, brief flashes on lotus leaves, and stretched into long strips by water ripples. Bridge shadows and water patterns reflect each other, creating a continuous and gentle visual echo. The camera smoothly tracks laterally with a slight downward tilt, ensuring the full path of light diffusion remains coherent.

Shot 7 connects to the previous shot through a fade-in/fade-out spatial expansion, ultimately pulling back to a wide-angle elevated but nearly level view. The pavilion, misty bridge, lotus pond, distant mountains, and clouds all enter the frame. Soft foreground mist and flowering branches create a gentle framing. In the midground, the elder remains standing calmly at the pavilion. In the background, the entire paradise is progressively illuminated by flowing caustic spots. Red walls, bridge surfaces, pond water, and mist all display fine, dynamic light patterns. Focus gradually shifts from the character to the entire space being lit. The light is not harsh but warm and luminous, filtered through water and mist. The final guqin note gently fades, coinciding with the last light spot dissolving into the mist. The camera continues to pull back smoothly with a slight upward tilt, concluding the optical demonstration in serene and ethereal silence.
